key_insight: Ceramic performance is controlled by the full processing–microstructure–property chain, where atomic bonding and defects dictate the trade-off between extreme hardness/stability and brittle fracture.
engineering_relevance: The review highlights how sintering, sol–gel, and additive manufacturing can be used to tune density, porosity, phase stability, and biofunctionality for structural and biomedical ceramic design.
method: Conventional sintering for densification and grain growth control
Sol–gel processing for composition and microstructure tailoring
Additive manufacturing for geometry, porosity, and multimaterial architectures
evidence_signal: This is a review article synthesizing reported relationships across ceramic systems rather than presenting a single new experimental dataset or benchmark.
watch_item: A major implementation concern is the porosity–strength trade-off and sensitivity to flaws, residual stresses, and processing heterogeneity.
paper_title: Ceramic Materials: From Atomic Bonding and Processing to Microstructure, Functional Properties, and Biomedical Applications
